issue.title: [Bug] `xfyun/spark-x2.6`: a base64 image in a `function_call_output` is counted as a ~167k-token turn, and every later request in that conversation fails with upstream `400 invalid_prompt`
issue.body:
## Summary

Codex → magpie → 讯飞 (xfyun) `spark-x2.6` on Windows 10.

After one screenshot landed in a **tool result** (`function_call_output`), magpie's own prompt
accounting for that conversation went from ~85k to ~225k tokens, of which **one single turn is
167,598 tokens**. From that point on, every request for that conversation comes back from the
upstream as

```
400 {"code":"invalid_prompt","message":"invalid request"}
```

in about 1.1 s — before any output. The client (Codex) only ever shows `invalid request`, and the
conversation cannot be recovered inside the client: the oversized turn stays in the history, so
each retry resends it.

Two things look wrong from the outside:

1. **The image is counted as text.** A 1.63 MB base64 PNG inside a tool result measures as 167,598
   prompt tokens (≈10.2 characters per token), i.e. it is being tokenized as the raw base64 string,
   not as an image. magpie *did* run vision descriptions for the same requests (see below), yet the
   turn did not shrink — the original payload is apparently kept alongside/instead of the
   description.
2. **No window metadata for this model.** `xfyun/spark-x2.6` is the only one of the 218 entries in
   `GET /v1/models` without `context_length` / `context_window` / `max_input_tokens`
   (217 have it, e.g. `group/*` report 1000000). Codex therefore has nothing to size the window
   against, and its own estimate stayed at ~85k while magpie measured 225k — so its
   `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 110000` never fired.

## Environment

- magpie **0.1.1578**, `magpie-windows-amd64.exe` (Windows x64, 60,623,872 bytes,
  sha256 `DF8D3177834525D98DC3D89B7DC54D585B531B594F292A725D24D3223FEE7F91`), running as the app
  (window + tray), PID 10196, gateway on `127.0.0.1:3425`, `GET /` reports `"models":218`.
- Windows 10 26H2, build 26300.9711, AMD64.
- Agent: **Codex**, `model = "xfyun/spark-x2.6"`, `model_provider = "magpie"`,
  `wire_api = "responses"`, `base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"`.
- magpie setting `"vision": "group/qianwen"` (default), provider `xfyun` (single model
  `spark-x2.6`, `native_endpoints: ["/v1/chat/completions","/v1/responses","/v1/messages"]`).

## Timeline (all times +08:00, from `~/.config/magpie/routing/2026-10-26.jsonl`)

The `prompt_tokens` column is what magpie itself computed and reported for the request:

| time | prompt tokens | turns | largest single turn | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12:21:55 | 82,870 | 25 | 14,370 | 200 |
| 12:22:35 | 84,399 | 25 | 14,934 | 200 |
| 12:22:40 | 85,141 | 25 | 15,001 | 200 — *the screenshot enters a `function_call_output` here* |
| 12:23:27 | 67,666 | 25 | 11,618 | first `invalid request` |
| 13:09:15 | **223,672** | 26 | **167,598** | `400 invalid_prompt` |
| 15:55:26 | 222,172 | 27 | 167,598 | `400 invalid_prompt` |
| 15:58:03 | 222,288 | 28 | 167,598 | `400 invalid_prompt` |
| 16:02:16 | 225,402 | 29 | 167,598 | `400 invalid_prompt` |
| 16:02:42 | 225,427 | 30 | 167,598 | `400 invalid_prompt` |
| 16:08:45 | 225,435 | 31 | 167,598 | `400 invalid_prompt` |

Earlier the same model accepted a **130,096-token** prompt on the same account
(11:38:20, `in=128240 cache_read=1856`, `200`, 176 s). So the boundary is somewhere between ~130k
and ~223k; the exact limit is unknown to the client because the catalog entry has no
`context_length`.

Upstream timing on the failures (`tries[].net`), 16:02:16:

```json
{"connect":2.2,"tls":56.8,"send":177.9,"wait":772.5,"head":1434.4}
```

The whole body was sent in ~178 ms and the 400 came back ~0.7 s later — this is an immediate
rejection of the payload, not an upload timeout or a hung connection.

## The 167,598-token turn

From the Codex session rollout (captured before the conversation was deleted in the client):

```
response_item -> function_call_output (2026-10-26T04:22:40Z = 12:22:40+08:00)
  line size 1.63 MB
  output[0] = {"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo..."}
```

1.63 MB ≈ 1.71 M characters; 1.71 M / 167,598 ≈ **10.2 characters per token** — the size of the
turn matches a plain-text tokenization of the base64 string.

For comparison, in the 484 Codex routing records of 2026-10-25/26 only 6 have a single turn above
80k tokens, and all 6 are this same turn in its failing state; 450 of 484 are below 20k.

## Vision did run — and did not shrink the turn

`usage.jsonl`, same session, same requests:

```
15:55:26  codex  qwen3.8-flash  kind=vision  200  in=1724  out=944   11756ms
15:55:26  codex  qwen3.8-flash  kind=vision  200  in=2694  out=1103  12475ms
15:58:04  codex  qwen3.8-flash  kind=vision  200  in=188   out=800   23639ms
15:58:04  codex  qwen3.8-flash  kind=vision  200  in=134   out=1317  38278ms
```

So two images were described successfully (descriptions of 800–1317 output tokens), and the main
request still measured 167,598 tokens for that turn and was still rejected. That is the part I
cannot explain from the outside: either the raw `output` of the tool result is kept next to the
description, or images inside `function_call_output` are not replaced at all.

## What the client sees

Codex's own log for the failing turns (`~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite`):

```
16:02:44  Request completed method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/responses
          status=200 OK  headers={"content-type": "text/event-stream", "x-magpie-model": "xfyun/spark-x2.6",
          "x-magpie-provider": "xfyun", ...}
16:02:44  Turn error: invalid request
```

So magpie answers **HTTP 200** and then reports the failure as an in-stream error whose message is
the upstream's own string, `invalid request`. The client has no status code, no code, no
`param`, and no indication that the cause is size. (Related: #3427 discusses diagnostic fields
being dropped on the Chat route; this is the native Responses route, so the message survives — it
is just not actionable.)

## What I would like to see

1. **Advertise the window** for `xfyun/spark-x2.6` in `GET /v1/models` (`context_length` /
   `max_input_tokens`), like the other 217 entries, so clients can trim or compact before sending.
2. **Check the prompt against that window before calling upstream** and fail with something
   actionable — which part is over, its size, the limit — instead of relaying a bare
   `invalid request`. Trimming the oldest turns, or at least warning, would keep a long
   conversation usable.
3. **Look at the 167,598-token turn**: an image inside `function_call_output` that measures at
   ~10 characters per token means the base64 is being counted/sent as text. If images in tool
   results are supposed to go through the vision describer like images in user messages, this one
   is not being replaced.

## Minimal repro (partial)

Text only, works — the model and the gateway are fine:

```bash
curl -sS -N http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/responses \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer magpie' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"xfyun/spark-x2.6","stream":true,"max_output_tokens":32,
       "input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"say ok"}]}]}'
```

An image inside a tool result:

```bash
curl -sS -N --max-time 100 http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/responses \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer magpie' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"xfyun/spark-x2.6","stream":true,"max_output_tokens":24,
       "input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"hello"}]},
                {"type":"function_call","name":"view_image","call_id":"c1","arguments":"{}"},
                {"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"c1",
                 "output":[{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="}]}]}'
```

Observed on this machine (it did not reach an upstream 400, so it is not the full repro of the
report): magpie starts a vision description, and with a 1×1 PNG that description took >95 s and
the caller gave up. With a 40 s timeout the same shape returned

```
agent=curl model=xfyun/spark-x2.6 status=502 err="image not described"
agent=curl model=qwen3.8-max    kind=vision status=499 err="the agent canceled the request"
```

I could not make the size-driven `invalid_prompt` happen with a small synthetic prompt, because I
do not know the model's limit and did not want to burn a ~200k-token request on a real account.
The evidence above is from a real conversation.

## Attachments

- `evidence-routing.jsonl` — every magpie routing record of the affected Codex session
  (`prompt.tokens`, turns, largest turns, per-try status/error). Account names, key ids, host names
  and the title-link hashes removed.
- `evidence-usage.jsonl` — the matching `usage.jsonl` rows (status, tokens, latency, error,
  endpoint), same redaction.
- `codex-routing-all.jsonl` — all 484 Codex routing records of 2026-10-25/26 with the largest
  single turn and any vision call within ±90 s, for comparison.
- `summary.json` — counts behind the table above.

---

## Attachments (download)

The full report is bundled as a gist (the raw per-file evidence jsonl dumps were removed;
available on request):

- Gist: https://gist.github.com/fanyuxaun386/668f2d7390c00bac966d2e54863231eb

comments.body:
The turn was counted and sent as its base64: the tool result arrived as a `data:image/png;base64,…` URL in the tool's **text**, so `internal/gateway/prompt.go` sized it with `tokensOf` (670,392 characters at about four characters a token is exactly the 167,598-token turn in your routing log), and `internal/gateway/image_input.go`'s `walkImages` only looked for images inside block lists, so the vision description replaced nothing and the base64 went upstream as a prompt. That is why the turn never shrank and why `spark-x2.6` answered `invalid_prompt` on every later request.

The branch treats such a result as the picture it is: counted as an image, and for a model that can't see images described in place by the vision model (or left out where the description fails), as an image block in a tool result already was. It covers the sibling shapes too — a Responses `function_call_output` string output, `custom_tool_call_output`, `local_shell_call_output`, a tool's text block, a Chat `tool` message, an Anthropic `tool_result` and a Gemini `functionResponse` part.

[fix/3724-xfyun-spark-x2-6-a](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3724-xfyun-spark-x2-6-a), commit 3603d9190aaff61cb7d6736874d9d2a613f5483d

Run at that commit: `TestToolResultImageURLInTextIsTheImage` fails without the change (`the turn is counted as its base64: Tokens:167609`, and the base64 was in what the text-only model was sent) and passes with it; `gofmt -l` on the changed files, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./internal/gateway/` print nothing. `go test ./internal/gateway/ -count=1` was killed while still running, so the full package suite is **not** verified by this branch.

This is a fork branch, ready to review; it makes no claim on the issue's ownership. Not in it: the `context_length` for `xfyun/spark-x2.6` (its window comes from the vendor's own model list or models.dev, and neither states one here) and any pre-flight size check with a more actionable error.

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body: 报错 通过 magpie 反代转发到华为云 CodeArts / InferHub 后端时，请求返回 HTTP 400： 本轮运行失败400: {"code":"InferHub.001001005.400","message":"CodeArts: The request param is invalid, Please check it (InferHub.001001005.400)","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"} 环境 - 客户端 / 调用方式：DeepSeek Harness → 本地 magpie（127.0.0.1:31425，group/deepseek） - magpie 版本：待补充 - 失败的上游路由：华为云 iam 账号（体验版），iam:cf0a4a90…:user:hid_0v2s586v6tgt5f55 - 该华为账号额度：0.73 / 5,500 积分（已用 0%，32 小时后重置）——额度充足，可排除欠费/限流 关键对照（定位要点） 同一次调用、同一个 magpie 下的其他上游路由全部正常： - 用户0565808085 Credits → DeepSeek-V4-Flash-max / v4.1-flash-max / V4-Flash-Official-max / V4-Pro-Official-max / V4-Pro-max：均 273.14 / 2,600 积分（已用 11%），正常返回。 失败时 magpie 面板中该华为路由状态显示为「400 · 失败 · 已交给 DeepSeek Harness」（触发 failover 回退后才继续）。 ⇒ 问题只出在华为云 CodeArts / InferHub 这一条 provider 路由，DeepSeek 系列路由不受影响。高度怀疑是 magpie 转发给 InferHub 的请求参数/格式不被该后端接受。 现象 - 华为云 iam（体验版）路由稳定返回 400（invalid_request_error），依赖 DeepSeek Harness 侧 failover 才能完成调用。 - DeepSeek Credits 系列路由无此问题。 期望 - 定位是哪一个请求参数被 InferHub 判定为 invalid（字段缺失 / 命名不符 / 格式问题？）。 - 确认 magpie 转发给 CodeArts / InferHub 的请求体是否需要针对该后端做适配。 - 如属配置问题，盼给出可用的华为云 CodeArts / InferHub provider 配置示例。 补充 愿意配合提供更详细的请求日志或抓包，如需特定信息请告知。
